TechCrunch (2012-07-15, BV Capital's rename to e.ventures) says the firm had run five separate regional funds, each under its own name, with a dedicated local team; Eastern Europe's became 'e.ventures Russia'. That supports a separate Russia fund rather than the main funds, but no fund vehicle, legal entity or manager name for it was found. Pre-2012 Russian deals (Heverest.ru, Feb 2012) name the investor as 'eVenture Capital Partners', which the same period's press also uses for the firm's global umbrella (Fight My Monster: 'other investments include Groupon, Angie's List and Sonos'), so that name does not identify the Russia vehicle. The Moscow deals in this packet (Heverest.ru, Teamo) were both Fast Lane Ventures incubator companies.
